sourceLegend.MP §n: Master prompt (project brief dated 2026-10-01), section n
sourceLegend.REF p.n: Reference handwritten system design notes, 'Page n of 15' (docs/reference/system-design-notes/)
sourceLegend.PROPOSED: Added by RequirementAgent during analysis; NOT present in source material; requires explicit approval before status APPROVED

priorityLegend.P0: Must - required for the first production release (v1.0.0): core ordering path, security, data integrity, mandated engineering governance
priorityLegend.P1: Should - mandated by the brief but not on the core ordering path; may slip to v1.x without blocking ordering
priorityLegend.P2: Could - from reference notes or proposed; backlog until product confirmation

evidenceGates.ANALYSIS->APPROVED: Named human approver recorded; all PROPOSED items explicitly accepted or removed
evidenceGates.DEVELOPMENT->CODE_REVIEW: Linked pull request; tests for every acceptance criterion exist
evidenceGates.CODE_REVIEW->TESTING: PR approved by CodeReviewAgent and a human reviewer; CI green
evidenceGates.TESTING->UAT: Test-run evidence: commit SHA, environment, executed/passed/failed counts, report link; zero failed
evidenceGates.UAT->READY_FOR_RELEASE: UAT sign-off recorded; regression suite for impacted areas passed
evidenceGates.READY_FOR_RELEASE->RELEASED: Release record (SemVer) with deployment evidence and smoke-test results
evidenceGates.RELEASED->COMPLETED: Traceability row complete: backend, web, mobile (where applicable), tests, release

versioningRules: Requirement IDs are immutable and never reused, including after CANCELLED
Any change to a requirement's content creates version N+1; version N is kept unchanged in changeHistory
A new version re-enters ANALYSIS and requires an impact report (REQ-RMS-004) before APPROVED
Changes that break existing behaviour require explicit approval before implementation
History is append-only; deleting or rewriting earlier versions is not permitted

requirements.title: Requirement registry with unique IDs and full schema
requirements.description: Every requirement is stored in a central registry with a unique immutable ID and the complete requirement schema.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Phase 1: Git-versioned requirements.json validated by a JSON Schema in CI. Phase 18: requirement-service indexes the same data for APIs and the admin dashboard.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: IDs match ^REQ-[A-Z]+-[0-9]{3}$ (NFR-[A-Z]+-[0-9]{3} for non-functional) and are unique across the registry.
AC2: A requirement missing any mandatory schema field fails validation and the CI build.
AC3: Requirements can be filtered by ID, module, status, priority, phase and release.
AC4: A cancelled requirement's ID is never reassigned.
apiRequirements: Phase 18: GET /api/v1/requirements, GET /api/v1/requirements/{id}, POST, PATCH (approver role)
uiRequirements: Phase 18: Admin > Requirements list and detail
securityRequirements: Changes only via reviewed pull requests; API writes restricted to approver roles

requirements.title: Immutable requirement versioning and change history
requirements.description: Requirement changes create new versions; history is never overwritten.
requirements.technicalRequirement: changeHistory array is append-only; CI compares against the main branch and rejects edits or deletions of earlier versions.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Changing any content field creates version N+1 while version N remains readable unchanged.
AC2: Each version records author, date, summary, reason and approver.
AC3: A pull request that modifies or removes an earlier version entry fails CI.
AC4: A new version re-enters ANALYSIS status.
uiRequirements: Version timeline with diff between versions

requirements.title: Requirement status workflow with evidence gates
requirements.description: Status changes follow the defined transition table, and key transitions require evidence.
requirements.technicalRequirement: statusModel.transitions and statusModel.evidenceGates in this file are the rule set; validated in CI and later by requirement-service.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Only the 15 allowed statuses are accepted.
AC2: A transition not present in the transition table is rejected.
AC3: TESTING->UAT is rejected without a linked test-run evidence record showing zero failures.
AC4: RELEASED->COMPLETED is rejected unless the traceability row is complete.
AC5: Every transition records actor, timestamp, from, to and reason.
securityRequirements: Only approver role may move ANALYSIS->APPROVED and READY_FOR_RELEASE->RELEASED

requirements.title: Requirement change impact analysis
requirements.description: Every requirement change produces an impact report before implementation.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Impact report template (Markdown + JSON) stored under docs/requirements/impact/; generated by DevAgent analyzeImpact() from Phase 18, manually by RequirementAgent before that.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: The impact report lists affected services, APIs, DB tables, web screens, mobile screens, tests and documentation.
AC2: Breaking changes (API contract, destructive schema change, removed behaviour) are flagged and require recorded approval before implementation starts.
AC3: The report is linked to the new requirement version.
AC4: The regression suite for impacted areas is identified and must pass before TESTING->UAT.
testingRequirements: Impact report generation test against a sample change

requirements.title: Requirement traceability matrix
requirements.description: Each requirement is traceable to backend, web and mobile implementation, tests and status.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Matrix generated from requirement IDs referenced in code annotations/test names and CI test reports; never hand-edited.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: The matrix shows, per requirement, backend, web, mobile, tests and status columns.
AC2: The matrix is regenerated on every merge to develop/main.
AC3: A requirement with no linked automated test cannot move beyond TESTING.
AC4: Mobile/web columns show '-' only when the requirement declares no UI/mobile scope.
testingRequirements: Matrix generator test with fixture repository

requirements.title: Release management with semantic versioning
requirements.description: Each release has a complete record with evidence and a rollback plan.
requirements.technicalRequirement: docs/releases/<version>.md + releases.json; SemVer; release notes generated from linked requirements and conventional commits.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: A release record contains version, date, requirements, features, bug fixes, breaking changes, DB changes, migrations, deployment status, test status and rollback plan.
AC2: A release cannot be marked deployed to production without staging smoke-test evidence.
AC3: Release notes are generated, not hand-written, from requirements and commits.

requirements.title: API Gateway: routing, versioning, correlation, CORS, security headers
requirements.description: Single entry point for all client traffic with routing, authentication, rate limiting, tracing and security headers.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Spring Cloud Gateway; routes /api/v1/<context>/**; JWT validation via identity-service JWKS (enabled in Phase 5); X-Correlation-Id generated if absent; access logging.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: /api/v1/{auth,users,restaurants,menu,cart,orders,payments,delivery,...}/** route to the owning service via discovery.
AC2: Protected routes without a valid JWT return 401 in the standard error format; public routes (register, login, OTP, public browse, payment webhook) are explicitly allow-listed.
AC3: Every response carries X-Correlation-Id and the same ID appears in downstream service logs.
AC4: HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options and Referrer-Policy headers are present on all responses.
AC5: CORS allows only origins configured for the environment.
apiRequirements: Version prefix /api/v1; future breaking versions /api/v2 routed side by side
securityRequirements: Strip spoofable internal headers (e.g. X-User-Id) from inbound requests

requirements.title: Service discovery, health checks and client-side load balancing
requirements.description: Services register dynamically, expose health and are load-balanced by logical name.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Spring Cloud Netflix Eureka (see open question OQ-15 for Kubernetes-native alternative); Spring Cloud LoadBalancer; Actuator liveness/readiness groups.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: A service registers on startup and deregisters on graceful shutdown.
AC2: An instance failing health checks stops receiving traffic within 30 seconds (PROPOSED value).
AC3: Inter-service calls use logical service names and are balanced across 2+ instances.
AC4: /actuator/health/liveness and /actuator/health/readiness are exposed per service.

requirements.title: Centralised configuration and secret management
requirements.description: Configuration is centralised per environment and secrets are never hard-coded.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Spring Cloud Config Server (Git-backed) for non-secret config; secrets via environment variables locally and a secret manager (e.g. AWS Secrets Manager/Vault via External Secrets) in staging/production.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: No credential, JWT key, API key, payment key, AI key or Redis/Kafka/DB password exists in source control; CI secret scanning fails the build on detection.
AC2: Services load profile-specific config (local, dev, staging, prod).
AC3: Changing a non-secret config value does not require rebuilding images.
AC4: A service fails fast at startup when required configuration is missing.
mobileRequirements: Mobile/web builds contain only public configuration (API base URL, public keys)
securityRequirements: Config server requires authentication; secrets encrypted at rest

requirements.title: Standard API contract: error format and OpenAPI documentation
requirements.description: Consistent error responses and complete OpenAPI documentation for every API.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Shared error library with @RestControllerAdvice; springdoc-openapi per service, aggregated at the gateway; generated TypeScript clients for web/mobile.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Every error response is {success:false, code, message, timestamp, traceId, details?} with a stable machine-readable code.
AC2: Stack traces, SQL, and internal class names never appear in responses (negative tests).
AC3: Validation failures return 400 with field-level details.
AC4: Each endpoint's OpenAPI entry documents method, request, response, validation, authentication, required permissions, error codes and an example.
AC5: Breaking contract changes require a new version path and an approved impact report (REQ-RMS-004).
apiRequirements: Error code catalogue per service (e.g. ORDER_NOT_FOUND, INVALID_ORDER_TRANSITION)
uiRequirements: Clients map error codes to user-friendly messages
mobileRequirements: Same error code mapping as web
securityRequirements: No sensitive data in error messages

requirements.title: Event backbone: versioned events, idempotent consumers, retry and DLT
requirements.description: Kafka-based asynchronous communication with a standard event envelope and reliable consumption.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Kafka (KRaft). Topic per aggregate (e.g. order.events.v1) keyed by aggregateId; envelope {eventId, eventType, eventVersion, occurredAt, producer, aggregateType, aggregateId, correlationId, causationId, payload}; consumer group per service; retry topics with backoff; <topic>.dlt.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Every event carries the standard envelope including eventId and eventVersion.
AC2: Re-delivering an already processed eventId has no additional effect (processed_events check).
AC3: Events for the same aggregate are consumed in production order.
AC4: A poison message moves to <topic>.dlt after the configured retries and raises an alert.
AC5: Schema changes within a major event version are backward compatible; breaking changes publish a new version.
testingRequirements: Testcontainers Kafka tests: duplicate delivery, ordering, DLT routing
securityRequirements: Kafka ACLs per service principal in staging/production

requirements.title: Transactional outbox and idempotency keys
requirements.description: State changes and their events are committed atomically; mutating APIs are safe to retry.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Outbox table written in the same local transaction as the state change; relay publishes to Kafka. Idempotency-Key header stored with request hash and response.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: When Kafka is unavailable, state changes still commit and their events are published after recovery; no event is lost (failure test).
AC2: Order, payment, refund and wallet mutating endpoints require an Idempotency-Key.
AC3: A repeated request with the same key and payload returns the original response without re-executing.
AC4: The same key with a different payload returns 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.
AC5: Idempotency records expire after a configurable TTL (PROPOSED default 24 h).
apiRequirements: Idempotency-Key header documented on mutating endpoints
uiRequirements: Clients generate one key per user action and reuse it on retry
mobileRequirements: Same as web; keys persisted across app restarts for in-flight actions
performanceRequirements: Outbox relay publish delay p95 < 1 s (PROPOSED)

requirements.title: Resilience for synchronous calls
requirements.description: Synchronous dependencies are protected with timeouts, retries and circuit breakers where justified.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Resilience4j applied per call site with a documented reason; bulkheads only for external providers.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Every outbound synchronous call has an explicit timeout.
AC2: Calls to payment gateway, maps, SMS/email/push providers and LLM are behind circuit breakers with defined fallbacks.
AC3: Retries are applied only to idempotent operations, with exponential backoff and jitter.
AC4: Breaker state and retry counts are exported as metrics.
uiRequirements: Degraded-mode messages when a dependency is unavailable

requirements.title: Persistence standards: database-per-service, migrations, audit columns, optimistic locking
requirements.description: Each service owns its PostgreSQL database with versioned, backward-compatible migrations.
requirements.technicalRequirement: PostgreSQL per service (PostGIS where geospatial); Flyway; JPA base entity with id (UUID), created_at, updated_at, created_by, updated_by, version (@Version).
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: No service connects to another service's database (enforced by separate credentials).
AC2: Migrations run automatically and follow expand/contract so version N-1 of the app keeps working.
AC3: Core entities include id, created_at, updated_at, created_by, updated_by, version.
AC4: Updating an entity with a stale version returns 409 CONFLICT.
AC5: Money is stored as DECIMAL(12,2) with currency code; floating point is never used for money.
databaseRequirements: Separate logical databases: identity_db, user_db, restaurant_db, menu_db, cart_db, promotion_db, order_db, payment_db, delivery_db, location_db, notification_db, review_db, search_db, recommendation_db, ai_db, media_db, admin_db, analytics_db, audit_db
performanceRequirements: Connection pool sizing documented per service

requirements.title: Registration and login with JWT access token and rotating refresh token
requirements.description: Users register and log in; services authenticate requests with locally verifiable JWTs.
requirements.technicalRequirement: identity-service issues RS256 access tokens (PROPOSED 15 min) and opaque refresh tokens (PROPOSED 30 days) stored hashed with family-based reuse detection; JWKS endpoint for verification.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: A customer registers with name, email and/or phone and password; a duplicate email/phone returns 409 USER_ALREADY_EXISTS.
AC2: Passwords are hashed with Argon2id or BCrypt; plaintext is never stored or logged.
AC3: Login returns an access token and a refresh token; invalid credentials return 401 without revealing which field was wrong.
AC4: Refresh rotates the refresh token; reusing a rotated token revokes the whole token family.
AC5: Downstream services validate access tokens via JWKS without calling identity-service per request.
databaseRequirements: identity_db: users (credentials), roles, permissions, user_roles, role_permissions, refresh_tokens
uiRequirements: Login and registration screens with client-side validation (React Hook Form + Zod)
securityRequirements: Web: access token in memory, refresh token in HttpOnly Secure SameSite cookie
Key rotation supported via JWKS kid
performanceRequirements: Login p95 < 500 ms excluding hashing cost tuning

requirements.title: OTP verification and OTP login
requirements.description: Phone numbers are verified and users can log in with a one-time password.
requirements.technicalRequirement: OTP stored hashed in Redis with TTL; sent through notification-service SMS adapter.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: OTPs are 6 digits, single-use and expire after 5 minutes (PROPOSED).
AC2: At most 5 verification attempts per OTP and 3 sends per 15 minutes per phone (PROPOSED); exceeding returns 429.
AC3: A phone number must be verified before the first order is placed (PROPOSED).
AC4: OTP values never appear in logs, traces or error messages.
databaseRequirements: Redis: otp:{purpose}:{phone} hashed value + attempt counter
mobileRequirements: SMS auto-read where the platform allows (Android SMS Retriever)
testingRequirements: Expiry, reuse, attempt-limit and rate-limit tests
securityRequirements: Generic responses that do not reveal account existence

requirements.title: RBAC with granular permissions and resource ownership checks
requirements.description: Access is controlled by role-mapped permissions plus ownership of the target resource.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Permissions embedded in JWT claims (or resolved by role); @PreAuthorize with permission checks; ownership checks in the application layer of each service.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Roles CUSTOMER, RESTAURANT_OWNER, RESTAURANT_MANAGER, DELIVERY_PARTNER, ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN, SUPPORT_AGENT exist.
AC2: Permissions (e.g. ORDER_CREATE, ORDER_CANCEL, ORDER_VIEW, ORDER_REFUND, RESTAURANT_UPDATE, MENU_UPDATE, USER_BLOCK) are mapped to roles as data, not hard-coded per endpoint.
AC3: Each endpoint declares required permissions; a missing permission returns 403.
AC4: Customers access only their own orders, restaurant staff only their restaurants/branches, partners only their assigned deliveries (IDOR tests).
AC5: Role/permission changes are audited and only SUPER_ADMIN can grant ADMIN or SUPER_ADMIN.
databaseRequirements: identity_db: roles, permissions, role_permissions, user_roles (with scope: restaurant_id/branch_id)
uiRequirements: Navigation and actions hidden when permission is absent (server still enforces)
testingRequirements: IDOR tests for every resource type

requirements.title: Session management, logout and password reset
requirements.description: Users manage sessions, log out and reset passwords securely.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Refresh token revocation; short-lived reset tokens; session list derived from refresh token records.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Logout revokes the current refresh token; 'log out all devices' revokes all of the user's refresh tokens.
AC2: Users can list active sessions with device and last-used time.
AC3: Password reset uses a single-use token/OTP expiring in 15 minutes (PROPOSED); the response never reveals whether the account exists.
AC4: Changing the password revokes all other sessions.

requirements.title: Brute-force protection and account lockout
requirements.description: Authentication endpoints resist credential stuffing and brute force.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Redis counters per identifier and per IP; temporary lockout; audit events.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: After 5 failed logins within 15 minutes (PROPOSED), login for that account is locked for 15 minutes and the user is notified.
AC2: Auth endpoints are rate limited per IP and per identifier.
AC3: Lockouts and suspicious login events are written to the audit log.
uiRequirements: Clear lockout message with retry time
securityRequirements: Lockout must not enable trivial denial of service (unlock via OTP)

requirements.title: Customer profile and food preferences
requirements.description: Customers maintain profile details and food preferences used by search, recommendations and AI.
requirements.technicalRequirement: user-service owns profiles and preferences; publishes UserPreferencesUpdated; preferences cached in Redis.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: A customer can view and update name, email, phone and profile image; changing email/phone requires re-verification.
AC2: Preferences include diet (VEG, NON_VEG, VEGAN, EGGETARIAN), preferred cuisines, spice level and price range.
AC3: Updating preferences publishes UserPreferencesUpdated.
mobileRequirements: Profile image from camera or gallery
securityRequirements: Only the owner (and support with permission) can view profile PII

requirements.title: Customer address book with geo-coordinates
requirements.description: Customers manage delivery addresses with coordinates used for serviceability and routing.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Addresses stored with PostGIS point; order-service snapshots the address at order creation.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: A customer can add, edit and delete addresses with label, lines, landmark, city, pincode, latitude and longitude.
AC2: Exactly one address can be the default; delivery addresses require coordinates.
AC3: Editing an address does not change addresses already snapshotted on past orders.
AC4: A customer can store at most 20 addresses (PROPOSED).
uiRequirements: Location selection with map pin and address search
mobileRequirements: Current location via GPS to prefill address
securityRequirements: Addresses are PII; visible to assigned partner only during active delivery

requirements.title: User device registration for push notifications
requirements.description: Apps register devices and push tokens so users can receive push notifications.
requirements.technicalRequirement: user_devices table; notification-service resolves tokens via user-service API or replicated read model.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: After login, the app registers device ID, platform, push token and app version; token refreshes update the record.
AC2: Logout or a provider 'invalid token' response deactivates the device.
AC3: A user can have multiple active devices.
mobileRequirements: Capacitor Push Notifications plugin registration flow
securityRequirements: Push tokens never exposed to other users

requirements.title: Favourite restaurants and products
requirements.description: Customers save favourite restaurants and dishes for quick access.
requirements.technicalRequirement: favourites table in user-service; availability resolved at read time via search read model.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: A customer can favourite and unfavourite restaurants and products; the operation is idempotent.
AC2: Favourites are listed with current availability; unavailable items are shown as unavailable rather than removed.
uiRequirements: Heart toggle on restaurant and product cards; Favourites screen

requirements.title: Restaurant onboarding with document verification and admin approval
requirements.description: Owners register restaurants, upload compliance documents and go live after admin approval.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Restaurant onboarding state machine in restaurant-service; documents via media-service private storage.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: An owner submits legal name, address, geo location, contact, cuisines and uploads GST and FSSAI documents.
AC2: Onboarding states DRAFT -> SUBMITTED -> UNDER_REVIEW -> APPROVED | REJECTED, and operational states ACTIVE | SUSPENDED; invalid transitions are rejected.
AC3: Only ADMIN can approve, reject (reason required) or suspend.
AC4: Only APPROVED and ACTIVE restaurants are visible to customers.
AC5: Approval, rejection and suspension are audited and notify the owner.
securityRequirements: Documents private; signed URL access for owner and admins only

requirements.title: Restaurant profile, branches and operational settings
requirements.description: Restaurants maintain profile data and one or more branches; a branch is the orderable outlet.
requirements.technicalRequirement: restaurant_branches with PostGIS location and delivery radius; RestaurantUpdated/BranchUpdated events feed search.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Owner/manager can update description, images, cuisines, cost for two, packaging fee, average preparation time, delivery radius (km) and auto-accept setting.
AC2: A restaurant can have multiple branches, each with its own address, location, hours, settings and menu availability.
AC3: Changes publish events consumed by search-service.
AC4: Managers can modify only branches they are assigned to.

requirements.title: Opening hours, holidays and live open/closed availability
requirements.description: Branches define schedules and can open/close manually; customers cannot order from closed branches.
requirements.technicalRequirement: restaurant_hours with multiple slots per day and date overrides; computed open status cached in Redis; BranchAvailabilityChanged event.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Weekly hours support multiple slots per day plus holiday/date overrides, evaluated in the branch time zone.
AC2: A manual open/close toggle overrides the schedule until the next slot boundary or until reverted.
AC3: Checkout for a closed branch fails with RESTAURANT_CLOSED.
AC4: Open status changes are reflected in search results within 60 seconds (PROPOSED).

requirements.title: Restaurant staff management
requirements.description: Owners invite and revoke managers scoped to their restaurant or specific branches.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Invitations in restaurant-service; role assignment with scope performed through identity-service API.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: An owner invites a manager by email/phone; on acceptance the invitee gets RESTAURANT_MANAGER scoped to the chosen branches.
AC2: Revoking a staff member blocks their access on the next request (scope re-checked server side).
AC3: Managers cannot invite staff, change ownership-level settings or delete the restaurant.

requirements.title: Menu categories and products
requirements.description: Restaurant staff manage categories and products with prices and dietary attributes.
requirements.technicalRequirement: menu-service owns categories and products per restaurant (shared across branches with branch-level availability); MenuUpdated events.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Staff can create, edit, reorder and deactivate categories and products (name, description, price, veg flag, spice level, preparation time, tags, images).
AC2: Prices are DECIMAL INR; every price change is audited with old and new values.
AC3: Deactivated products are hidden from customers but retained for order history.
AC4: Changes publish MenuUpdated events.
uiRequirements: Menu management screens with drag-and-drop ordering

requirements.title: Product variants and add-ons with selection rules
requirements.description: Products support variants and grouped add-ons with min/max selection rules.
requirements.technicalRequirement: product_variants and product_addons (addon groups with min/max); rules validated by cart-service using menu-service data.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: A product can have variants (e.g. Half/Full), each with its own price.
AC2: Add-on groups define min and max selections and per-add-on price.
AC3: Cart rejects selections that violate min/max rules with INVALID_ADDON_SELECTION.
uiRequirements: Product customisation sheet for customers; editor for staff

requirements.title: Product availability and inventory
requirements.description: Staff control item availability per branch, with optional stock counts and availability windows.
requirements.technicalRequirement: product_availability per branch (flag, optional stock quantity, time windows); MenuItemAvailabilityChanged event; stock decremented on OrderConfirmed.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Staff can mark an item available/unavailable per branch; the change is visible to customers within 30 seconds (PROPOSED).
AC2: Optional stock quantity is decremented on order confirmation; reaching 0 marks the item unavailable.
AC3: Availability windows (e.g. specific hours) are respected by menu reads and checkout validation.
AC4: Availability changes publish MenuItemAvailabilityChanged.
uiRequirements: One-tap out-of-stock toggle on live orders and menu screens

requirements.title: Menu read performance and cache invalidation
requirements.description: Customer menu reads are served from cache and invalidated correctly on change.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Cache-aside in Redis keyed by branch; eviction after transaction commit; TTL as safety net.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: A branch's full customer menu is served from Redis with a TTL of 10 minutes (PROPOSED, within REF p.5 range 5-15 min).
AC2: Any menu, price or availability change evicts affected cache entries after the transaction commits.
AC3: A cache outage degrades to database reads without errors.
AC4: Menu read p95 < 300 ms under the target load (NFR-PERF-001).

requirements.title: Location-aware restaurant discovery
requirements.description: Customers see approved, serviceable restaurants near their location.
requirements.technicalRequirement: search-service queries its PostGIS-enabled read model using ST_DWithin against each branch's delivery radius.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Given coordinates, results include only APPROVED and ACTIVE branches whose delivery radius covers the location.
AC2: Closed branches are excluded or shown as 'opens at <time>' according to a request flag.
AC3: Each result includes distance, ETA estimate, rating, cost for two and offer badge.
AC4: Results use cursor-based pagination.
mobileRequirements: Uses device GPS or selected address

requirements.title: Text search, filters and sorting
requirements.description: Customers search by restaurant, dish or cuisine and refine results with filters and sorting.
requirements.technicalRequirement: PostgreSQL full-text search plus pg_trgm similarity for typo tolerance; filter/sort executed in the read model.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Search matches restaurant names, dish names and cuisines, tolerating minor typos.
AC2: Filters: cuisine, veg-only, minimum rating, price range, max delivery time, has offers.
AC3: Sorts: relevance, distance, rating, delivery time, cost, popularity.
AC4: Queries shorter than 2 characters return 400 rather than unbounded scans.
databaseRequirements: search_db: dish_search_docs; GIN indexes on tsvector and trigram
uiRequirements: Search bar with suggestions; filter chips; sort menu

requirements.title: Search read model synchronisation and engine portability
requirements.description: Search owns a denormalised index fed by events, behind an interface that allows OpenSearch later.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Consumes Restaurant/Menu/Review/Availability events; SearchIndex port with PostgreSQL adapter; rebuild job; Redis cache for popular queries.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Source changes appear in search results within 60 seconds (PROPOSED).
AC2: All search access goes through a SearchIndex interface; an OpenSearch adapter can replace PostgreSQL without API changes.

requirements.title: Order state machine with guarded transitions and history
requirements.description: Order status is governed by an explicit state machine; invalid transitions are rejected.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Enum-based state machine in the domain model with transition table and role guards; optimistic locking on orders. Full table: docs/architecture/order-state-machine.md.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Happy path: CREATED -> PAYMENT_PENDING -> CONFIRMED -> RESTAURANT_ACCEPTED -> PREPARING -> READY_FOR_PICKUP -> DELIVERY_ASSIGNED -> PICKED_UP -> OUT_FOR_DELIVERY -> DELIVERED. A partner assigned during preparation is recorded on the order immediately (deliveryPartnerId, partnerAssignedAt) and the order moves to DELIVERY_ASSIGNED automatically when it reaches READY_FOR_PICKUP.
AC7: If the assigned partner is released (unassigned), the order moves DELIVERY_ASSIGNED -> READY_FOR_PICKUP and reassignment starts.
AC2: Failure states PAYMENT_FAILED, RESTAURANT_REJECTED, CANCELLED, DELIVERY_FAILED, REFUND_PENDING, REFUNDED are reachable only from the states defined in the transition table.
AC3: Any other transition returns 409 INVALID_ORDER_TRANSITION.
AC4: Each transition is authorised by role (e.g. only restaurant staff for PREPARING, only assigned partner for PICKED_UP).
AC5: Every transition is stored in order_status_history (actor, timestamp, reason) and publishes the matching event.
AC6: Concurrent transitions on one order resolve via optimistic locking; exactly one succeeds.
testingRequirements: Exhaustive transition table tests (valid and invalid)
Early-assignment test: partner assigned in PREPARING, order auto-moves to DELIVERY_ASSIGNED on READY_FOR_PICKUP

requirements.title: Delivery assignment engine with scoring
requirements.description: The engine selects the most suitable partner using a documented, configurable scoring model.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Candidate search via Redis GEO (GEOSEARCH); hard filters then weighted score; offer with timeout; distributed lock per order; decision log.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Assignment starts on RESTAURANT_ACCEPTED, timed so the partner's ETA to the restaurant approximates remaining preparation time; it starts immediately at READY_FOR_PICKUP if not yet assigned.
AC2: Hard filters: ONLINE, verified, below capacity, not stale, within search radius (start 2 km, expand to 5 km per REF p.9).
AC3: Score = weighted sum of normalised distance, ETA, workload/availability, rating and acceptance rate; weights configurable (defaults 40/20/10/20/10 per REF p.9).
AC4: Offers expire after 30 seconds (REF p.9); on reject/timeout the next candidate is offered; a partner never receives the same order twice.
AC5: Exactly one partner is assigned per order under concurrency; DeliveryAssigned is published.
AC6: If no partner accepts within the maximum radius/attempts, AssignmentFailed is published and ops are alerted.
AC7: Candidate scores and the decision are logged for explainability.

requirements.title: AI food assistant: natural language to structured search criteria
requirements.description: Customers describe what they want in natural language; the assistant converts it to validated criteria and returns real results.
requirements.technicalRequirement: ai-service uses LLM structured output constrained by a JSON schema; results always come from search/recommendation tools.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: 'I want spicy vegetarian food under 300 rupees' produces {diet: VEGETARIAN, spice: HIGH, maxPrice: 300} that validates against the criteria schema.
AC2: Ambiguous or unsupported requests produce a clarifying question instead of guessed criteria.
AC3: Every restaurant, dish and price in a response exists in tool results for that turn (no fabricated items; verified by evaluation set).
AC4: Conversation context is kept within a session.
uiRequirements: Chat panel with result cards and quick add-to-cart
mobileRequirements: Chat screen; voice input optional later
testingRequirements: Golden evaluation set for criteria extraction

requirements.title: Controlled tool execution (no direct database access)
requirements.description: The LLM can act only through a registry of tools that call backend APIs with the user's permissions.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Tool registry in ai-service; tools call public APIs through the gateway using the caller's token; schema-validated inputs.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Only registered tools can be invoked (initially searchFood, getMenu, getRecommendations, addToCart, getOrderStatus).
AC2: Tools call backend APIs through the gateway with the end user's permissions; ai-service has no database credentials for other services.
AC3: Tool inputs are schema-validated; invalid tool calls are rejected and logged.
AC4: State-changing tools (e.g. addToCart) require explicit user confirmation in the UI.
AC5: Every tool call is logged with traceId, tool name and outcome.
securityRequirements: Least privilege; no order placement or payment tools in v1

requirements.title: AI guardrails, cost control and monitoring
requirements.description: The assistant resists prompt injection, minimises data sharing, controls cost and is observable.
requirements.technicalRequirement: System prompt isolation, output validation, red-team suite, PII minimisation, per-user rate limits, budget tracking, keyword-search fallback; metrics to Prometheus.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: A prompt-injection red-team test set runs in CI; no test can trigger a non-registered tool or reveal system instructions.
AC2: Only data needed for the request is sent to the LLM provider; payment data and contact details are never sent.
AC3: Per-user rate limits and a monthly cost budget are enforced; on provider failure or budget exhaustion the assistant falls back to keyword search.
AC4: Admin dashboard shows AI latency, token usage, cost, error rate and tool call distribution.

requirements.title: Media upload and delivery via object storage
requirements.description: Images and documents are stored in object storage; the database holds only metadata.
requirements.technicalRequirement: media-service issues pre-signed upload URLs (S3-compatible; MinIO locally), validates, scans, generates image variants, serves public images via CDN and private files via short-lived signed URLs.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Clients upload directly to object storage with pre-signed URLs; PostgreSQL stores only metadata.
AC2: Content type, extension and magic bytes are validated; size limits 5 MB for images and 10 MB for documents (PROPOSED).
AC3: Files pass a malware-scan hook before becoming visible.
AC4: Images are resized to standard variants and served via CDN.
AC5: Private documents (restaurant/partner KYC) are accessible only to the owner and admins via signed URLs expiring within 5 minutes (PROPOSED).
uiRequirements: Upload component with progress and validation errors
testingRequirements: File upload security tests (polyglot, oversized, wrong type)
securityRequirements: No public bucket listing; private bucket for documents

requirements.title: Administer users, restaurants and delivery partners
requirements.description: Admins search, review, approve, block and unblock platform participants.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Admin endpoints live in owning services; admin-service aggregates views where needed; all actions audited.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Admins list, search and filter users, restaurants and partners and view details.
AC2: Admins approve/reject restaurants and partners and block/unblock users (USER_BLOCK); blocking revokes all sessions.
AC3: Every admin action requires the relevant permission and is audited.
uiRequirements: Admin users, restaurants and partners screens

requirements.title: Order, payment, refund and coupon oversight
requirements.description: Admins investigate orders and payments, issue refunds and manage coupons.
requirements.technicalRequirement: admin-service aggregates order timeline (order, payment, delivery events) for a single view.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Admins search orders and payments and see a unified timeline across order, payment and delivery.
AC2: Admins issue full/partial refunds with reason; refunds above a threshold need SUPER_ADMIN approval (PROPOSED).
AC3: Admins manage platform coupons (REQ-PROMO-001).

requirements.title: Complaints and customer support
requirements.description: Customers raise complaints about orders; support agents triage and resolve them.
requirements.technicalRequirement: admin-service owns complaints (support tickets) with SLA timers.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: A customer can raise a complaint on an order with category, description and images.
AC2: Support agents assign, respond to and resolve complaints; statuses OPEN, IN_PROGRESS, RESOLVED, CLOSED.
AC3: Support agents can issue refunds within their permission limits.
AC4: SLA timers flag overdue complaints.
uiRequirements: Help on order detail; admin complaints queue

requirements.title: Engineering, system health and audit visibility in admin
requirements.description: Admins see requirement, development, test, deployment and production status, releases, system health, AI monitoring and audit logs.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Admin dashboard reads requirement-service, release records, Prometheus/health APIs and audit-service.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: For each requirement the admin sees requirement status, development status, test status, deployment status and production status.
AC2: Release list shows notes, status and evidence links.
AC3: System health panel shows service status and key metrics; AI monitoring panel per REQ-AI-003.
AC4: Audit log viewer supports filtering by actor, action, entity and date.
uiRequirements: Admin Requirements, Releases, System Health, AI Monitoring, Audit Logs screens

requirements.title: Business analytics and reports
requirements.description: Platform and restaurant KPIs are computed from events, never from operational databases.
requirements.technicalRequirement: analytics-service consumes domain events into analytics_db (partitioned PostgreSQL initially; warehouse later).
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: KPIs: orders, GMV, average order value, cancellation rate, payment failure rate, average delivery time, ETA accuracy, coupon usage.
AC2: Admin reports filter by date, city and restaurant and export to CSV.
AC3: Restaurant analytics: orders, revenue, top items, ratings, preparation time.
AC4: Analytics queries never run against operational service databases.
databaseRequirements: analytics_db: fact_orders, fact_payments, fact_deliveries, daily aggregates
uiRequirements: Admin reports; restaurant analytics dashboard with charts
securityRequirements: Restaurant sees only its own analytics
performanceRequirements: Report queries p95 < 2 s for 90-day range (PROPOSED)

requirements.title: Audit trail for sensitive operations
requirements.description: Every sensitive operation produces an immutable audit record.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Services emit AuditEvent via outbox in the same transaction; audit-service stores append-only records with hash chaining.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Refunds, user blocking, restaurant approval, price changes, role changes, permission changes and admin actions produce audit records.
AC2: Records contain actor, actor role, action, entity type and ID, old value, new value, timestamp, IP (where appropriate) and traceId.
AC3: The audit store has no update/delete API; records are hash-chained so tampering is detectable (PROPOSED).
AC4: A sensitive operation cannot commit without its audit event (same-transaction outbox).
AC5: Admins can search audit records; retention period per OQ-20.
testingRequirements: One audit test per sensitive operation
securityRequirements: Audit values mask secrets and full card/phone data

requirements.title: Shared design system for web and mobile
requirements.description: Centralised tokens and components give web and mobile a consistent look while respecting platform UX.
requirements.technicalRequirement: web/packages/ui: design tokens (Tailwind preset + CSS variables), React components, component catalogue with visual baselines.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Colours, typography, spacing, radius and shadows are defined once and consumed by all web and mobile apps.
AC2: Components: button, input, card, modal, toast, table, navigation, form controls, loading, empty and error states, each with documented variants.
AC3: Components meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast and keyboard accessibility (NFR-A11Y-001).
AC4: A component catalogue (e.g. Storybook) has visual regression baselines.
mobileRequirements: Platform variants (e.g. bottom sheets, safe areas, touch targets >= 44px)

requirements.title: Customer web application
requirements.description: Responsive React web app covering the full customer journey.
requirements.technicalRequirement: React + TypeScript + Vite, React Router, TanStack Query, Axios (generated client), Zustand, React Hook Form + Zod, Tailwind CSS.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Implements login, registration, location selection, discovery, search, filters, restaurant details, menu, product details, cart, coupon, address, checkout, payment, order tracking, order history, reviews, profile, wallet, notifications, favourites and recommendations (each backed by its module requirement).
AC2: Layout is responsive from 360 px width to desktop.
AC3: Payment success is shown only after server confirmation.
AC4: Order tracking polls until REQ-RT-002/003 deliver live updates in Phase 16.
AC5: Playwright covers the full ordering journey.

requirements.title: Restaurant dashboard
requirements.description: Web dashboard for owners and managers to run their restaurant.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Same web stack and design system; permission-aware navigation.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Implements dashboard, orders, live orders, menu management, categories, products, variants, add-ons, inventory, offers, restaurant profile, opening hours, analytics, reviews, staff and settings.
AC2: Live orders update without manual refresh (polling until Phase 16, WebSocket after).
AC3: Owner and manager see only the features their permissions allow.

requirements.title: Delivery partner web dashboard
requirements.description: Web dashboard for partners (primary partner experience is the mobile app).
requirements.technicalRequirement: Shares delivery feature modules with delivery-mobile where practical.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Implements online/offline, available orders, assigned orders, navigation links, pickup, delivery, earnings, history, profile and notifications.
AC2: Browser geolocation is used only while the tab is active; continuous background tracking requires the mobile app.

requirements.title: Admin dashboard
requirements.description: Web back-office for admins, super admins and support agents.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Same web stack; permission-based navigation; data tables with server-side pagination.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Implements users, restaurants, delivery partners, orders, payments, refunds, coupons, reports, analytics, complaints and audit logs (engineering screens via REQ-ADMIN-004).
AC2: Navigation and actions reflect the signed-in role's permissions; the server enforces all checks.
securityRequirements: Session timeout for admin users (PROPOSED 30 min idle)

requirements.title: Customer mobile application (React + Capacitor)
requirements.description: Native Android/iOS customer app with mobile-first UX, sharing logic and design system with web.
requirements.technicalRequirement: React + TypeScript + Capacitor; shared packages (ui, api-client, domain hooks); mobile-specific navigation and screens.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Builds for Android and iOS from one codebase, sharing design system, API client and domain logic with web.
AC2: Mobile UX: bottom-tab navigation, native-feeling transitions, pull to refresh, offline and poor-network states (not a wrapped website).
AC3: Native capabilities: GPS, push notifications, camera, secure storage, optional biometric unlock, deep links to restaurant and order.
AC4: Appium covers login, location permission, discovery, cart, checkout, order tracking and push.
mobileRequirements: Capacitor plugins: Geolocation, Push Notifications, Camera, Preferences/Secure Storage, App (deep links), Biometric (community plugin)
performanceRequirements: Cold start < 3 s on mid-range Android (PROPOSED)

requirements.title: Delivery partner mobile application with background location
requirements.description: Primary partner tool: offers, workflow, navigation and continuous location while online.
requirements.technicalRequirement: React + Capacitor; background geolocation (Android foreground service, iOS background location mode) with consent and battery-aware intervals.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Implements online/offline toggle, offers with countdown, assigned orders, navigation deep links, pickup/delivery actions, earnings, history, profile and notifications.
AC2: Background location runs only while ONLINE, after explicit consent with OS-compliant disclosures, and stops when OFFLINE.
AC3: Update interval adapts to movement and battery; updates are queued offline and flushed on reconnect.
AC4: Appium covers the delivery workflow end to end.
mobileRequirements: Store policy compliance for background location (Google Play, App Store)

requirements.title: DevAgent tool suite
requirements.description: An internal AI agent with tools to manage requirements, impact, tasks, code, tests, bugs, docs and releases.
requirements.technicalRequirement: ai-agents/dev-agent with a tool layer over requirement-service APIs, Git, CI and the test runner (language per OQ-18).
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Tools: getRequirement, createRequirement, updateRequirement, getRequirementHistory, analyzeArchitecture, analyzeImpact, createTask, updateTask, getTaskStatus, generateCode, reviewCode, generateTests, runTests, analyzeFailure, createBug, updateDocumentation, generateReleaseNotes.
AC2: Every tool action is recorded with task ID, requirement ID, input summary and output.
AC3: DevAgent reads the relevant .ai/ context files before modifying code.
testingRequirements: Tool contract tests with fixture repository

requirements.title: Governed change workflow for AI agents
requirements.description: Agents change code only through the approved workflow and can never bypass human approval.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Agents operate on feature branches and open PRs; branch protection and CI gates enforce the workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Major changes follow Requirement -> Impact Analysis -> Plan -> Implementation -> Tests -> Review -> Approval -> Merge.
AC2: Agents cannot push to main/develop, deploy, or read production secrets.
AC3: A requirement cannot be marked COMPLETED without evidence (REQ-RMS-003).
AC4: Reported test results must reference a real CI/test run ID.
testingRequirements: Policy tests: attempted direct push/deploy is denied
securityRequirements: Agent identity separate from human identities; all actions audited

requirements.title: Specialised agent handoff, shared state and standard output
requirements.description: Specialised agents share structured project state and report in a standard format.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Shared state via requirement-service + .ai/ context files; agent report JSON schema.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Agents: Architect, Requirement, Backend, Frontend, Mobile, Database, DevOps, Security, Test, Documentation, CodeReview, with the handoff order from MP §55.

AC2: Every agent returns TASK ID, REQUIREMENT ID, CURRENT STATUS, WHAT WAS ANALYZED, WHAT WAS CHANGED, FILES CHANGED, DATABASE CHANGES, API CHANGES, TESTS CREATED, TESTS EXECUTED, TEST RESULTS, KNOWN ISSUES, DEPENDENCIES, NEXT ACTION, validated by schema.
AC3: .ai/ contains project-context, architecture-context, requirements-context, coding-standards, testing-standards, security-rules, deployment-context, current-sprint and known-issues, kept current.

requirements.title: Test generation from acceptance criteria
requirements.description: TestAgent derives multi-layer tests from each requirement's acceptance criteria.
requirements.technicalRequirement: ai-agents/test-agent reads requirements.json, generates JUnit/REST Assured, Playwright and Appium tests tagged with requirement and AC IDs.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: For a requirement, TestAgent proposes backend unit, integration, API, web E2E, mobile E2E, negative, security and regression tests as applicable.
AC2: Each generated test references its requirement ID and AC number.
AC3: Generated tests enter the suite only through a reviewed pull request.
testingRequirements: Generation quality checked on sample requirements (e.g. REQ-ORDER-004)

requirements.title: Test execution, evidence recording and bug creation
requirements.description: TestAgent runs suites, stores evidence, files bugs on failures and updates traceability.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Parses JUnit XML / Playwright / Appium reports from CI; links evidence to requirements.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Evidence includes commit SHA, environment, executed/passed/failed/skipped counts, duration and report artefacts.
AC2: Failures are analysed; bugs are created and linked to requirement and test; the requirement moves to BUG_FOUND.
AC3: TestAgent never reports results for tests that were not executed.
AC4: The traceability matrix is updated after each run.
uiRequirements: Test status per requirement in admin (REQ-ADMIN-004)

requirements.title: Screenshot-based visual implementation and testing
requirements.description: Given a reference screenshot, the agent derives a UI spec, verifies the implementation visually and generates correction tasks.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Playwright screenshots at defined viewports; pixel diff (e.g. pixelmatch) and SSIM; per-screen thresholds; diff images stored as artefacts.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: From a reference image the agent records layout, spacing, typography, colours, components and responsive behaviour as a UI spec.
AC2: Implementation screenshots are captured at defined viewports and compared using a measured metric (pixel diff % and/or SSIM) against per-screen thresholds.
AC3: Differences produce diff images and correction tasks; the loop repeats until the threshold is met or escalates after N iterations.
AC4: Reports state the measured similarity; 'pixel-perfect' is never claimed without a 0% diff measurement.
testingRequirements: Comparator accuracy tests with known image pairs

requirements.title: Backend testing standards and coverage gates
requirements.description: Every backend service is tested across unit, integration, API, data, messaging, security and failure scenarios.
requirements.technicalRequirement: JUnit 5, Mockito, Spring Boot Test, Testcontainers (PostgreSQL, Kafka, Redis), REST Assured, WireMock; JaCoCo.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Each service has unit, integration, API, database, Kafka, Redis, security, transaction, concurrency and failure-scenario tests where applicable.
AC2: External providers are stubbed with WireMock; infrastructure uses Testcontainers, not shared environments.
AC3: CI enforces line coverage of at least 80% on domain and application layers (PROPOSED).
AC4: Test names or tags reference requirement IDs.

requirements.title: Web and mobile end-to-end test suites
requirements.description: Critical user journeys are automated end to end on web and mobile.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Playwright (web) and Appium/WebdriverIO (mobile) against seeded ephemeral or staging environments with the mock payment gateway.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Playwright covers login, search, restaurant selection, add to cart, checkout, payment, order tracking, cancellation, review and admin operations.
AC2: Appium covers login, location permission, restaurant discovery, cart, checkout, order tracking, push notification and delivery workflow.
AC3: Suites run in CI against seeded data; flaky tests are tracked and quarantined with an owner.

requirements.title: Performance testing and reports
requirements.description: Key flows are load tested and measured against NFR targets.
requirements.technicalRequirement: k6 as primary tool (JMeter/Gatling optional); runs against staging with production-like data volume.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Scripts exist for restaurant search, menu retrieval, cart, order creation, payment (mock gateway) and order tracking.
AC2: Reports include RPS, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, CPU, memory and database load.
AC3: Results are compared with NFR targets; regressions above 10% (PROPOSED) fail the performance gate.
AC4: No NFR is marked verified without a stored report.
securityRequirements: Never run load tests against production without approval

requirements.title: Security testing
requirements.description: The platform is tested against common attack classes in non-production environments.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Automated authz/IDOR suites, SAST, SCA, container and secret scanning in CI; OWASP ZAP DAST against staging.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Tests cover authentication bypass, authorization bypass, SQL injection, XSS, broken access control, rate limiting, JWT attacks (alg none, key confusion, expiry, tampering), IDOR, sensitive data exposure and file upload vulnerabilities.
AC2: SAST, dependency, container image and secret scans run in CI; DAST runs against staging only.
AC3: No destructive testing is performed against production.
AC4: Releases are blocked on unresolved critical/high findings.
securityRequirements: Findings tracked as bugs linked to requirements

requirements.title: Structured logging with correlation and PII masking
requirements.description: All services emit structured JSON logs carrying trace and correlation IDs, without secrets or PII. Scheduled in Phase 4 rather than Phase 20 (PROPOSED deviation, OQ-19).
requirements.technicalRequirement: Logback JSON encoder; MDC propagation; masking converters; central aggregation (Loki or ELK).
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Log lines are JSON with timestamp, level, service, traceId, spanId, correlationId, pseudonymised userId and message.
AC2: Passwords, OTPs, tokens, card data and full phone numbers never appear in logs (masking tests).
AC3: Logs from all services are searchable centrally by traceId.
testingRequirements: MDC propagation tests across async boundaries

requirements.title: Metrics, dashboards and alerting
requirements.description: Technical and business metrics are collected, visualised and alerted on.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Micrometer -> Prometheus; Grafana dashboards as code; Alertmanager rules.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Dashboards: API latency, error rate, order creation rate, payment failure rate, Kafka consumer lag, database performance, Redis performance, CPU and memory.
AC2: Alerts for SLO burn rate, error spikes, DLT growth, consumer lag and payment failure spikes.
AC3: Dashboards and alert rules are version-controlled.

requirements.title: Distributed tracing
requirements.description: Requests and events can be traced end to end across services.
requirements.technicalRequirement: OpenTelemetry (Micrometer Tracing bridge) exporting to Tempo or Jaeger; trace context in Kafka headers.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Traces span gateway, services and Kafka producers/consumers.
AC2: A complete order flow (create -> pay -> accept -> assign -> deliver) is viewable as linked traces.
AC3: Sampling is configurable per environment.

requirements.title: Production Dockerfiles and Docker Compose developer environment
requirements.description: Every service is containerised to production standards and the platform runs locally with Docker Compose.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Multi-stage builds, non-root user, minimal JRE base, HEALTHCHECK, env config; Compose with profiles (infra, core, all, observability).
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Each backend service has a multi-stage Dockerfile running as non-root on a minimal base image with a HEALTHCHECK.
AC2: docker compose starts PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, MinIO, a mail catcher and (optional profile) Prometheus/Grafana/Tempo/Loki.
AC3: Compose profiles allow running a subset of services to fit developer machines.
AC4: A new developer can start the platform with one documented command after installing prerequisites.
databaseRequirements: Local init script creates one database per service

requirements.title: CI pipeline and Git strategy
requirements.description: GitHub Actions builds, lints, tests, scans and packages every change; Git flow and conventional commits are enforced. Baseline CI from Phase 3 (PROPOSED deviation, OQ-19); full pipeline completed in Phase 23.
requirements.technicalRequirement: GitHub Actions with monorepo path filters; branch protection; commitlint.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Baseline (Phase 3): build, lint, unit tests and secret scan on every pull request.
AC2: Full (Phase 23): plus integration tests, SAST/SCA, Docker build and image push.
AC3: Branches main, develop, feature/*, bugfix/*, release/*, hotfix/*; main and develop are protected and require passing checks and review.
AC4: Commit messages follow Conventional Commits (feat, fix, test, docs, refactor, ...) and are validated in CI.
mobileRequirements: Mobile builds (Android/iOS) in CI from Phase 15
securityRequirements: Least-privilege workflow tokens; pinned action versions
performanceRequirements: PR pipeline < 15 min for a single-service change (PROPOSED)

requirements.title: Continuous delivery to development, staging and production
requirements.description: Deployments happen only through the pipeline, with approvals, smoke tests and rollback.
requirements.technicalRequirement: GitHub Environments with protection rules; rolling deployments on Kubernetes; automated smoke tests; rollback on failure.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Separate development, staging and production environments with separate config and secrets.
AC2: Deployments run only from the pipeline; local deployments are technically blocked (no local credentials).
AC3: Production deployment requires manual approval and passing staging smoke tests.
AC4: Failed post-deploy smoke tests trigger automatic rollback.
AC5: Deployments are zero-downtime (NFR-DEPLOY-001).
databaseRequirements: Migrations applied by pipeline before app rollout (expand/contract)
mobileRequirements: Mobile release via store pipelines (PROPOSED: Fastlane)
securityRequirements: OIDC federation from GitHub to cloud (no long-lived keys)

requirements.title: Kubernetes deployment design
requirements.description: Services run on Kubernetes in staging and production with autoscaling and health probes. Staging manifests in Phase 23 (needed by CD); production hardening in Phase 24.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Helm charts or Kustomize overlays per environment; External Secrets; Ingress controller; HPA; PDB.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Each service has Deployment, Service, ConfigMap, Secret (from external secret manager), Ingress where public, HPA, readiness and liveness probes, and resource requests/limits.
AC2: Manifests are templated per environment.
AC3: Critical services have PodDisruptionBudgets and run at least 2 replicas in production.
AC4: Kubernetes is not required for local development.

requirements.title: Infrastructure as code, backups and disaster recovery
requirements.description: Cloud infrastructure is reproducible and data is recoverable within defined objectives.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Terraform modules per environment (cloud per OQ-02); managed DB backups with PITR; DR runbook.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Network, Kubernetes cluster, managed PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka and object storage are provisioned by Terraform.
AC2: Automated backups with point-in-time recovery; a restore drill meets NFR-REL-002 and is repeated quarterly (PROPOSED).
AC3: A disaster recovery runbook is documented in docs/14-disaster-recovery.md.

requirements.title: Rate limiting
requirements.description: Traffic is rate limited at the gateway per user, IP and endpoint class.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Spring Cloud Gateway RequestRateLimiter with Redis token bucket; per-route policies.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Default limits per authenticated user and per IP; stricter limits for auth, OTP, coupon validation and AI endpoints.
AC2: Exceeding a limit returns 429 with Retry-After in the standard error format.
AC3: Limits are configurable per environment without redeploying.

requirements.title: Input validation and OWASP protections
requirements.description: Inputs are validated and the platform is protected against injection, XSS and CSRF.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Bean Validation on DTOs; JPA/parameterised queries only; output encoding and sanitisation of user content; CSP; CSRF tokens for cookie-authenticated endpoints.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: All request DTOs are validated; request body size limits are enforced.
AC2: Only parameterised queries are used; static analysis flags string-concatenated SQL.
AC3: User-generated content (reviews, names, complaints) is sanitised/encoded so stored XSS is not possible; web apps send a strict CSP.
AC4: Endpoints authenticated by cookie (refresh) are CSRF protected.
uiRequirements: React escaping by default; no dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitiser

requirements.title: Data protection and privacy
requirements.description: Personal and payment data are protected in transit and at rest and exposed only on a need-to-know basis.
requirements.technicalRequirement: TLS everywhere; encryption at rest (managed DB/storage) plus field-level encryption for KYC identifiers; role-based data minimisation in APIs.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: All external traffic uses TLS 1.2+; data at rest is encrypted; KYC document identifiers are field-level encrypted.
AC2: APIs return only data the caller's role needs (e.g. partners see customer details only during an active delivery).
AC3: Raw card data never reaches platform systems.
AC4 (PROPOSED, DPDP Act 2023 alignment): Users can request account deletion and data export; deletion anonymises personal data while retaining legally required financial records.
testingRequirements: Sensitive data exposure tests per endpoint
